tools.name: verify_email
tools.description: Check whether a single email address is deliverable using EmailVerifyFast (syntax, domain/MX and SMTP mailbox checks). Uses one verification credit. Waits up to wait_seconds for the result; if it is still running, returns a job_id to pass to get_results.

tools.name: verify_list
tools.description: Submit up to 500 email addresses as one EmailVerifyFast job (duplicates are removed; uses one credit per unique address). Waits up to wait_seconds; returns results if finished, otherwise a job_id and progress counts to use with get_results. For larger lists, split into batches or upload a CSV at htt

tools.name: get_results
tools.description: Fetch progress and results for a job_id returned by verify_email or verify_list. Results are paged (50 per page); optionally filter by status.

tools.name: check_credits
tools.description: Confirm the EmailVerifyFast API key works and summarise recent usage (lists and addresses submitted). The EVF API does not yet expose an exact remaining-credit balance; free accounts include 100 checks once, and the dashboard shows the exact balance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: verify_email, verify_list · Private data: check_credits · Public sink: verify_email, verify_list.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: verify_email, verify_list · Private data: check_credits · Public sink: verify_email, verify_list

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
